articles.title: Indoor gardening improves mental health and quality of life for cancer patients
articles.summary: Tending to indoor hydroponic gardens may help cancer patients improve their mental health and quality of life. A recent study found that growing salad greens at home eased depression symptoms and encouraged healthier eating habits among patients.

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Drug toxicity prediction is critical for reducing late-stage attrition in drug discovery, yet remains challenging due to severe class imbalance, scaffold-based generalization, and the clinical need for interpretable predictions. Single-modality approaches-SMILES Transformers or graph neural networks capture complementary aspects of molecular structure, while sequence-only models cannot directly provide graph-attributed explanations. articles.title: New study of Brazilian twins sheds light on the heritability of our creative confidence
articles.summary: A new behavioral genetics study of twins finds that about one-fifth of our belief in our own creativity is inherited. Ultimately, your unique individual experiences shape your creative confidence far more than your DNA.

articles.title: The neuroscience of pity: how attractiveness and morality shape empathy
articles.summary: New research explores how our brains react to seeing others in pain. The findings reveal that a person's physical attractiveness and moral history alter our empathy levels, shifting how our minds process compassion in fractions of a second.

articles.title: Emotional distress when stopping antidepressants appears to be due to withdrawal, not relapse
articles.summary: When people stop taking antidepressants, a sudden wave of anxiety or depression can feel like a devastating setback. But new research suggests these emotional spikes are usually a temporary physical withdrawal reaction, rather than a true relapse.

articles.title: Large analysis connects specific personality traits to problematic internet pornography use
articles.summary: A large review of past research has identified several personality traits, including impulsivity and neuroticism, that correlate with problematic internet pornography use. Conversely, traits like self-control and conscientiousness correspond with lower viewing rates overall.

articles.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
articles.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops. The finding suggests that dreaming may require such intense internal processing that neurons consume energy faster than it can be replenished.

articles.title: Scientists replace mouse cortex with human brain tissue to study neurological disorders
articles.summary: Scientists have successfully replaced the cortex of genetically modified mice with lab-grown human brain tissue. The transplanted human cells formed functioning circuits and responded to injury, offering a revolutionary new way to study human neurological disorders.

articles.title: Your worldview might dictate how you perceive neutral faces
articles.summary: A psychological study reveals that people who view the world as inherently dangerous consistently overestimate physical risks and view strangers as untrustworthy. This broad worldview predicts individual threat perception better than underlying anxiety or depression.

articles.title: A political shift decades in the making explains Trump’s grip on Congress
articles.summary: A new analysis challenges the narrative that Republican lawmakers back Donald Trump purely out of fear. Instead, decades of political realignment have created a unified base, meaning Congress and the president now answer to the exact same voters.

articles.title: This “rare” autism-linked genetic disorder may be far more common than scientists thought
articles.summary: A major analysis suggests Phelan-McDermid syndrome, a genetic disorder closely linked to autism, may affect about 1 in 7,300 people and more than 45,000 Americans. Researchers warn that thousands of cases may remain hidden because genetic testing is often not performed, even as targeted treatments move into clinical trials.

articles.title: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases
articles.summary: A large study tracking more than 95,000 people suggests that how you sleep may be linked to your risk of developing dozens of diseases. People who spent more time in REM sleep had lower risks of 83 conditions, including dementia, heart failure, and Parkinson’s disease, while more deep sleep was associated with lower risks of conditions such as type 2 diabetes and major depression.

articles.title: When what you see doesn’t make sense, your brain does something remarkable
articles.summary: The brain may have a built-in way to quickly settle disagreements between regions processing the same scene. Researchers found that matching signals between two visual areas lasted longer, while conflicting signals rapidly faded away. This “consensus building” mechanism could help explain how the brain turns many specialized inputs into one unified view of the world.
